content.title: About
content.content: Gala apples are sweet, aromatic fruits with a bright red stripe over a yellow‑green background. Consumed fresh, with skin, without any heat treatment. They provide vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber that support healthy nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Gala variety was developed in New Zealand in the 1930s and quickly gained worldwide popularity.
Gala apples contain a higher sugar content than many other varieties, making them especially sweet.
The skin is rich in antioxidants, so it is best left on.
The variety stores well at 0–4 °C for up to three months.
Gala apples are frequently used in juices, compotes, and desserts because of their versatile flavor.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Apples contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in the skin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to apples.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic apples, wash them thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

items.title: Stomach discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of apples can cause discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs due to fructose.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gala apples can be eaten whole, sliced into salads, added to oatmeal or yogurt, baked in pies, or juiced. Keeping the skin on preserves the maximum amount of nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store apples in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, in a perforated bag or an open container. At room temperature they keep for about a week but lose crispness and aroma more quickly.
